final_narrative:
The differentially-abundant metabolites map overwhelmingly to **Arachidonic Acid Metabolism** (KEGG map00590 / SMP SMP00075), with FDR effectively zero and fold-enrichment of ~643 across all matched compounds. Six of the eight input metabolites — arachidonic acid (C00219), Leukotriene A4 (C00909), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), 5,6-epoxy-8,11,14-eicosatrienoic acid (C14768), and 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ (C14717) — fall directly within this pathway. The two remaining compounds, 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (C00156) and 3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid (C01161), are phenolic acids not assigned to the arachidonic acid cascade in current database annotations, suggesting they arise from a parallel process.

**Key driver compounds** include arachidonic acid itself as the canonical entry point, and Leukotriene A4 as the branch-point from which the lipoxygenase arm diverges toward 5-HETE and 15-HETE. KEGG reaction-graph analysis confirms that arachidonic acid is connected to Leukotriene A4 via a two-hop path (C00219 → C05356 → C00909) and that Leukotriene A4 is subsequently upstream of 5-HETE through the same intermediate (C00909 → C05356 → C04805), consistent with the known enzymatic sequence of 5-lipoxygenase catalysis. 15-Deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ anchors the cyclopentenone prostaglandin arm derived from PGD₂ dehydration, while 5,6-epoxy-8,11,14-eicosatrienoic acid represents a cytochrome-P450 epoxygenase product of the same parent lipid.

**Biological significance** is substantial: arachidonic acid is the master precursor for eicosanoid synthesis, and coordinated changes in both its lipoxygenase and cyclopentenone branches suggest an inflammatory or resolution-phase stimulus. Elevated Leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE collectively point toward enhanced neutrophil chemotaxis and the initiation of specialized pro-resolving mediator pathways. 15-Deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ is a recognized PPAR-γ agonist with anti-inflammatory and pro-apoptotic properties, and its accumulation in this context may reflect a feedback attempt to suppress further leukocyte infiltration. The co-enrichment of 5,6-epoxy-8,11,14-eicosatrienoic acid indicates that the cytochrome-P450 epoxygenase arm is simultaneously activated, producing epoxyeicosatrienoic acids that antagonize pro-inflammatory signaling. Together, the metabolite signature is consistent with a treatment that drives coordinated multi-branch remodeling of the arachidonic acid cascade, likely involving COX/LOX inhibition or PPAR activation. The phenolic acids 4-hydroxybenzoic acid and 3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid may derive from gut-microbial or phase-II metabolism cross-talk but are not directly wired into the enriched eicosanoid network.
